posts.title: Previously On: Why We Started VFMBS
posts.author: The Board
posts.excerpt: The entertainment industry runs on deals. We wanted a place at Vanderbilt to learn how they get made.
posts.body:
Every great film has two scripts: the one on screen, and the one in the financing documents.

We started this society because we loved both, and couldn't find a place at Vanderbilt that taught the second one.

This season, we're doubling down: six workshop series, two industry treks and our biggest Greenlight Summit yet. Whether you're an Econ major who secretly writes screenplays or a film buff who's curious about spreadsheets, there's a seat for you.

posts.title: The Theatrical Window, Explained in Five Numbers
posts.author: Deal Desk
posts.excerpt: How long a film stays exclusive to cinemas is one of the most consequential numbers in Hollywood.
posts.body:
The theatrical window is the period a film plays exclusively in cinemas before it becomes available at home.

It used to be roughly three months. Today it's often closer to a month, and sometimes less. Shorter windows mean faster revenue from home entertainment, but they can also cannibalize ticket sales.

In our Box Office Analytics workshop, we build a simple model of that trade-off and see how the math shifts for a horror film versus a four-quadrant franchise.

reviews.q: I walked in knowing nothing about film finance. By December I was building slate models and talking waterfalls in interviews.
The Pitch Room finale was the most nerve-wracking and fun thing I've done at Vanderbilt.
Equal parts finance club and film club. That's exactly what I was looking for and couldn't find anywhere else.

faq.q: Do I need finance or film experience?
faq.a: No. Most members join with neither. Our workshops start from zero, and we care much more about curiosity and work ethic than your resume.
All of them. Our members come from Economics, CMA, Engineering, HOD, Film Studies, Math and more.

faq.q: How does the application process work?
faq.a: Submit the online application, then attend a 20-minute conversational interview. Decisions go out within a week of interviews.

faq.q: Can I attend events without being a member?
faq.a: Yes. Speaker events, screenings and the Greenlight Summit are open to all Vanderbilt students. Treks and some workshops are members only.
About 3–5 hours per week: one track meeting, one workshop session and whatever events you want to attend.
Workshops are open to everyone by application. Members get priority placement.
Membership is free for first-years; returning members pay modest semester dues that fund treks and events. Financial aid is available, just ask.

faq.q: How can my company partner with VFMBS?
faq.a: Visit our Partners page or email us. We work with studios, streamers, agencies, banks and funds on speaker events, treks, case competitions and recruiting.
